read_scope.notes: Read the complete 22-page frozen PDF, including references and Appendices A–G, using page-separated text extraction and visual inspection of every rendered page. Visually inspected Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–12. Consulted frozen paper.tex and specificity_results.tex to resolve wording and cross-references. Technical appendices were assessed as optional depth. No earlier manuscripts, other reviews, progress records, external sources or current non-snapshot manuscript were consulted.

score_reasons.expression: Excellent, precise English with unusually effective explanations of qualifications. Section 4.1 defines contrasts in ordinary language, gives an actual Monet–Sisley lightness example, and explains the 1/0/1 error benchmarks before the equations. Results consistently distinguish estimates from resolved comparisons and image measurements from perceptual judgments. Remaining wording refinements are localized, especially the abstract’s compression of near-zero and negative pair responses into “weak” alignment.
score_reasons.structure: The main text progresses coherently from the motivating ambiguity through reference and experimental design, feature interpretation, score intuition, inference, results and limits. Sections 5.1–5.5 make the sequence of findings visible, and Table 4 explains why averaging and calibration change the ordering. Retrospective diagnostics and historical cohorts have clearly marked roles; derivations and extensive checks are appropriately optional. One results cross-reference sends the reader to an incomplete subset of the comparisons it describes.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The reader can recover the experimental arms, finite digital reference target, scaling units, repeat correction, no-distinction benchmark and calibration operation without the repository. The examples preceding notation and captions specifying what projected agreement does and does not mean are especially successful. The abstract is standalone and the source-correction result is made concrete in Table 5. Only small local refinements are needed in the abstract’s description of pair direction and navigation to the full comparison family.
score_reasons.engagement: The consequential question is established immediately through the possibility of becoming closer to both Monet and Sisley without reproducing their distinction. Figure 1 provides an inspectable visual intervention; Figure 2’s common-scale detail panels and Figure 3’s annotated pair scores reward closer inspection. The near-unit response with substantial error, the averaging reversal, and the calibration reversal give the results a clear narrative. Claims remain restrained without losing the significance of these measured distinctions.

strengths: Section 4.1, page 5, makes an unfamiliar contrast-based evaluation understandable through the measured lightness gap and three simple benchmark generators before introducing indexed notation.

Sections 3.1–3.3 and 4.2 explicitly identify finite reference reproductions, separate development scaling, exact prompt arms, and the theoretical status of D = 1; these remove several plausible misunderstandings for a new reader.

Figures 1–3 are legible and purposeful: the example grid shows all conditions, the geometry plot supplies magnified Monet/Sisley/Pissarro views, and the pair heatmaps directly label their numerical benchmarks.
Sections 4.4 and 5.4 explain exactly what calibration changes, how the held-out scenes are used, and why the resulting ordering does not imply better images or statistical superiority.

Section 5.5 and Table 5 preserve the distinction between the original inferential family and retrospective source correction, including the changed Sunburst comparison and the absence of human verification.
The 10-page main narrative stands on its own, while the remaining pages preserve technical derivations, source provenance and supporting cohorts without requiring them for the central story.

findings.issue: The statement that the other 13 model-pair intervals include zero points to Table 2, but Table 2 displays only the five FLUX comparisons. The complete set of 15 model pairs is in Table 10.
findings.reader_effect: A reader checking the stated count cannot reconcile it with the immediately cited table and must discover the full table independently.
findings.suggested_change: Keep Table 2 for the FLUX comparisons, but change the citation attached to “the other 13 intervals include zero” to “Appendix E, Table 10,” or explicitly cite both tables. This requires no additional evidence or space.

findings.location: Abstract, page 1; paper.tex lines 36–37; Figure 3, page 8
findings.issue: “Weak Monet–Sisley alignment in five models” compresses two qualitatively different observations: near-zero positive responses and negative responses, including Sunburst’s −.249. The main results and figure explain the sign correctly.
findings.reader_effect: An abstract-only reader may understand all five models as showing a small response in the correct direction and miss that three estimated responses have the opposite sign.
findings.suggested_change: Replace “weak Monet–Sisley alignment” with “near-zero or reversed Monet–Sisley alignment.” This preserves the descriptive/retrospective status and adds only two words to the approximately 152-word abstract, remaining within the 155-word limit.

summary: An excellent, self-contained account of a bounded comparison of measured digital painter contrasts. The main narrative, estimands, visual evidence and diagnostic limitations are readily understood. The remaining changes are small wording and cross-reference repairs; no consequential restructuring or additional evidence is needed for editorial clarity.
